subject: Clarify: how token rounding and long-context billing are calculated
messages:

Subject: Questions on billing math for long-context calls

Hi Sergio,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Orion's engineering and ML teams are excited. Before we move to signature, finance and legal asked for one more reconciliation on how you meter long-context requests and how rounding/minimums are applied. Two concrete examples they gave: 1) a single API call with ~18,200 tokens (prompt + model output) and 2) many short streaming calls that cumulatively hit ~18,200 tokens in a day.

Specifically we need to confirm:
- Are those 18,200 tokens billed exactly, or rounded up to a quantum? If rounded, what's the quantum and rounding rule?
- Do KV cache / prefix reuse reduce billed units for repeated calls with shared context? How is that reflected on invoices?
- For streaming responses, is there a per-call minimum or do you aggregate per-session?

I've attached our proposed sample invoice (proposed-pricing-matrix.xlsx) showing how our accounting team expects to see items. Call out any differences and any concessions you can offer for the first quarter after launch.

Best,
Sam

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@orionretail.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Alicia Reyes <legal@orionretail.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 10:05:13 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on billing math for long-context calls

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear examples, and great questions. I summarized the behavior below and attached a short PDF with worked examples (redwood-billing-examples.pdf). High level answers first, then the math.

High level
- Billing unit: we meter "charged tokens" at the model level. For most models we report raw tokens used but invoice tokens are grouped into a billing quantum of 256 tokens for generation models and 1 token for embeddings. The 256-token quantum only applies to generation tokens (output + input) when the call is charged under per-token pricing.
- Rounding: we round up to the nearest quantum per billed call. For a single call with 18,200 tokens to a generation model that uses 256-token quantum, that call is rounded up to 18,432 tokens (256 * ceil(18,200 / 256)).
- Aggregation/streams: streaming responses are billed per request. We do not automatically aggregate separate HTTP requests into a single invoice line unless they are part of the same session and you enabled session aggregation (an opt-in feature on Dedicated and in some pilot agreements).
- KV cache/prefix reuse: KV cache reduces compute and therefore affects the runtime cost. For billing we credit repeated prefix tokens when the same exact prefix is reused within a window (default 24h). The credit is applied as a separate invoice line item labeled "KV reuse credit" and reduces billed tokens equivalent to the matched prefix length, up to the original billed amount.

Worked example (single call)
- Raw tokens: 18,200
- Quantum: 256
- Charged tokens: 256 * ceil(18,200 / 256) = 18,432
- Invoice shows: Model: rw-gen-13b, Raw tokens: 18,200, Charged tokens: 18,432, Rate: $0.0008/token, Line total: $14.746

Worked example (many small streaming calls)
- If you make 182 streaming calls of ~100 tokens each in the same session and session aggregation is disabled: each call is rounded to 256 → each call billed as 256 tokens → total charged tokens = 256 * 182 = 46,592 even though raw sum is 18,200.
- If session aggregation is enabled for that customer (we can enable on Dedicated or as a commercial term), we aggregate the raw tokens for the session first and then apply quantum rounding once: ceil(18,200 / 256) * 256 = 18,432.

Concessions / pilot recommendation
- For onboarding pilots we can: a) enable session aggregation for Orion for the first 90 days so you are billed close to raw usage, and b) issue a one-time KV reuse credit cap of 200k tokens for the first month to offset warm-up costs.
- Also happy to offer a 7% overage credit (applied as invoice-level discount) for the first billing cycle if you sign within two weeks.

Next steps
- Kim (CC) from pricing/legal — can you confirm if the session-aggregation activation needs a contract amendment or can be documented in the SOW? Sam, if that looks reasonable I can hand this to our contracts team and attach a short addendum to the PO.

Thanks — hope this removes the fog. See attached for a step-by-step sample invoice with line-item math.

— Sergio Alvarez
Sr. Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Sam,
Quick note from pricing/legal side: session aggregation is a toggled operational feature. For Hosted, we can enable it at the tenant level but we require an SOW addendum for billing treatment (so invoices reflect aggregated rounding). For Dedicated/Private, it's configurable via your admin console and does not require amendment — we will log the configuration change and include audit timestamps.

Regarding the pilot credits Sergio proposed: the KV reuse credit and the 7% overage credit are fine. We do need to cap the KV reuse credit (we suggested 200k tokens) and set an expiration (30 days). I'll draft the addendum language and share a clean DocuSign link. Alicia — if you could confirm the PO # and whether Orion needs the addendum to reference a specific SOW, we'll include it.

Kim
Kimberly Park
Pricing & GTM Operations — Redwood Inference
